newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli soldiers arrest pregnant woman in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldiers arrest pregnant woman in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli soldiers arrested a pregnant Palestinian woman in the West Bank town of Hebron on Tuesday, leaving neighbours to care for her nine children, Palestinians said.
They said five-month pregnant Monowwar Zaro was hauled off by the Israeli troops after they broke into her house and found an old rifle.

Neighbours said when they tried to persuade the soldiers to release Zaro they were told she would be released once her husband turned himself in. Palestinians said the husband, Shakir Zaro, was not a member of a militant group.
The Israeli army said it could not comment on the incident and said it was under police jurisdiction. The police spokesman was not immediately available to comment.

The PLO and Israel blamed one another on Tuesday for stalled talks on an Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron. The redeployment, according to a deal signed by Israel's previous government, was to occur in March.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who ousted the previous government in May elections, is demanding more security for some 400 Jews who study and live in Hebron amidst 100,000 Palestinians. The PLO refuses to make changes in the signed deal.
